title: Two Sum
summary: Practice trading a little extra memory for a faster search through a sequence.

prompt.description: Write a function that finds two different positions in an integer list whose values add up to a given target. Return the positions in either order, and assume one valid pair exists.

examples.explanation: The values at positions 1 and 3 total 8.
The values at positions 0 and 2 total 2.

constraints: The list contains at least two integers.
Do not use the same position twice.
Aim for better than checking every pair when possible.

title: Valid Parentheses
summary: Use a last-in-first-out structure to reason about nested delimiters.

prompt.description: Given a string made only of bracket characters, decide whether every opening bracket is closed by the matching type in the correct nested order.

examples.explanation: Each pair closes in reverse order of opening.
The closing bracket types do not match the nesting order.

constraints: The input contains only (), [], and {} characters.
An empty string is valid.

title: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock
summary: Track a running opportunity while scanning time-ordered values once.

prompt.description: Given daily prices for one asset, choose one day to buy and a later day to sell. Return the largest positive gain, or zero if no profitable trade is possible.

examples.explanation: Buying at 2 and selling later at 10 gives a gain of 8.
Every later price is lower than the earlier prices.

constraints: There is at least one recorded day.
The buy day must come before the sell day.
Prefer a single left-to-right pass.

title: Binary Search
summary: Narrow a sorted search space by repeatedly choosing a midpoint.

prompt.description: Create a function that locates a target in an ascending integer list. Return its position when present, or -1 when the target is absent.

examples.explanation: The target is stored at position 3.
The target does not occur in the list.

constraints: The input list is sorted in ascending order.
All values are distinct.
Aim for logarithmic search time.

title: Merge Intervals
summary: Order ranges and combine neighboring spans when their boundaries overlap.

prompt.description: Given a collection of numeric ranges, combine ranges that share any values and return the resulting non-overlapping ranges in ascending order.

examples.explanation: The first two ranges overlap and form one range.
The ranges are separate and are returned in order.

constraints: Each range has a start no greater than its end.
Input ranges may be in any order.
Touching endpoints count as overlapping.

title: Contains Duplicate
summary: Detect whether any value occurs more than once.

prompt.description: Given an integer list, return true if any value appears at least twice and false if every value is distinct.

examples.explanation: The value 1 appears twice.

constraints: The list may be empty.
Values may be negative.

title: Valid Anagram
summary: Compare character frequencies to determine whether two strings use the same letters.

prompt.description: Given two lowercase strings, return whether one can be rearranged to form the other.

examples.explanation: Both strings have the same character counts.

constraints: Strings contain lowercase English letters.
Different lengths cannot be anagrams.

title: Product of Array Except Self
summary: Combine products on either side of each position without dividing.

prompt.description: Return an array where each position contains the product of every input value except the value at that position. Do not use division.

examples.explanation: Each output is the product of the other three values.

constraints: The output must be computed without division.
Use O(n) time.

title: Maximum Subarray
summary: Find the contiguous range with the greatest sum.

prompt.description: Given an integer array, return the largest sum obtainable from any non-empty contiguous subarray.

examples.explanation: The range [4, -1, 2, 1] has sum 6.

constraints: The array is non-empty.

title: Maximum Product Subarray
summary: Track how negative values can turn a small product into a large one.

prompt.description: Given an integer array, return the largest product of any non-empty contiguous subarray.

examples.explanation: The subarray [2, 3] has product 6.

constraints: The array is non-empty.
Values may be negative or zero.

title: Find Minimum in Rotated Sorted Array
summary: Use the rotation boundary to search a sorted array efficiently.

prompt.description: An ascending array of distinct values was rotated an unknown number of times. Return its minimum value in logarithmic time.

examples.explanation: The rotation places the minimum at index 4.

constraints: The array is non-empty.
All values are distinct.
Aim for O(log n) time.

title: Search in Rotated Sorted Array
summary: Search a rotated sorted sequence by identifying its ordered half.

prompt.description: Search for a target in an ascending array that was rotated at an unknown pivot. Return its index, or -1 if absent.

examples.explanation: The target is at index 4.

constraints: All array values are distinct.
Aim for O(log n) time.

title: 3Sum
summary: Find unique triples whose values sum to zero.

prompt.description: Return every unique triplet of distinct indices whose values sum to zero. Do not include duplicate triplets in the result.

examples.explanation: These are the unique value triplets summing to zero.

constraints: A triplet must use three different positions.
The result must not contain duplicate triplets.

title: Container With Most Water
summary: Choose two boundaries that hold the greatest possible amount of water.

prompt.description: Each array value is the height of a vertical line. Choose two lines that, together with the x-axis, contain the maximum area.

examples.explanation: The lines at indices 1 and 8 hold area 7 * 7.

constraints: Choose two different indices.
The area is limited by the shorter line.

title: Sum of Two Integers
summary: Use bitwise operations to add integers without arithmetic addition.

prompt.description: Return the sum of two integers without using the plus or minus operators.

examples.explanation: Combine the sum bits and carry bits using bitwise operations.

constraints: Do not use the + or - operators.

title: Number of 1 Bits
summary: Count the set bits in an unsigned integer.

prompt.description: Given an unsigned integer, return the number of bits set to 1 in its binary representation.

examples.explanation: The binary representation is 1011.

constraints: The input is treated as an unsigned 32-bit integer.

title: Counting Bits
summary: Build bit counts for every number using results from smaller values.

prompt.description: Given a non-negative integer n, return an array where each index i contains the number of set bits in i.

examples.explanation: These are the set-bit counts for values 0 through 5.

constraints: Aim for O(n) time.

title: Missing Number
summary: Recover the absent value from a complete integer range.

prompt.description: An array contains distinct values from 0 through n with exactly one value missing. Return the missing value.

examples.explanation: The range 0 through 3 is missing 2.

constraints: The array contains n distinct values from [0, n].

title: Reverse Bits
summary: Reverse the order of the bits in a fixed-width integer.

prompt.description: Reverse the bits of a 32-bit unsigned integer and return the resulting unsigned value.

examples.explanation: The output is the integer represented by the reversed 32-bit sequence.

constraints: Process exactly 32 bits.

title: Climbing Stairs
summary: Count paths formed by taking one or two steps at a time.

prompt.description: How many distinct ways can you reach step n if each move climbs either one or two steps?

examples.explanation: There are five ordered combinations of one- and two-step moves.

title: Coin Change
summary: Find the fewest coins needed to make a target amount.

prompt.description: Given coin denominations and an amount, return the minimum number of coins needed to make that amount, or -1 if it cannot be made.

examples.explanation: The amount can be made with 5 + 5 + 1.

constraints: Each denomination is a positive integer.
You may use each denomination any number of times.

title: Longest Increasing Subsequence
summary: Find the length of the longest strictly increasing subsequence.

prompt.description: Given an integer array, return the length of its longest strictly increasing subsequence. The selected values need not be adjacent.

examples.explanation: One longest subsequence is [2, 3, 7, 101].

constraints: The array may contain duplicate values.

title: Longest Common Subsequence
summary: Compare prefixes to find the longest sequence shared by two strings.

prompt.description: Given two strings, return the length of their longest subsequence present in both. Characters in a subsequence keep their order but need not be adjacent.

examples.explanation: "ace" is a common subsequence.

constraints: Strings contain lowercase English letters.

title: Word Break
summary: Determine whether a string can be segmented into dictionary words.

prompt.description: Given a string and a dictionary of words, return whether the string can be split into a space-separated sequence of one or more dictionary words.

examples.explanation: The string splits into "leet" and "code".

constraints: A dictionary word may be reused.

title: Combination Sum
summary: Enumerate unique combinations that reach a target using reusable candidates.

prompt.description: Return all unique combinations of candidate values that sum to a target. A candidate may be chosen repeatedly.

examples.explanation: Both combinations total 7.

constraints: Candidate values are distinct positive integers.
The result must not contain duplicate combinations.

title: House Robber
summary: Maximize a sum while never choosing adjacent values.

prompt.description: Each value is the amount of money in a house along a street. Return the most money that can be taken without taking from adjacent houses.

examples.explanation: Taking houses with values 2, 9, and 1 totals 12.

constraints: Values are non-negative.

title: House Robber II
summary: Adapt the non-adjacent maximum when the first and last houses are neighbors.

prompt.description: Houses form a circle, so the first and last are adjacent. Return the maximum amount that can be taken without choosing neighboring houses.

examples.explanation: Only the middle house can be chosen alongside neither neighbor.

constraints: Values are non-negative.

title: Decode Ways
summary: Count valid letter decodings while accounting for zeroes and two-digit codes.

prompt.description: Digits map to letters 1 through 26. Return the number of ways a digit string can be decoded, where a leading zero or an invalid zero pairing is not allowed.

examples.explanation: The decodings correspond to 2|2|6, 22|6, and 2|26.

constraints: The string contains only digits.
The answer fits in a 32-bit signed integer.

title: Unique Paths
summary: Count routes through a grid when movement is limited to right and down.

prompt.description: A robot starts at the top-left of an m by n grid and may move only right or down. Return the number of distinct ways to reach the bottom-right.

examples.explanation: There are 28 distinct right/down paths.

title: Jump Game
summary: Track the farthest reachable index to determine whether the end is accessible.

prompt.description: Each value gives the maximum forward jump length from that index. Return whether the final index is reachable from the first.

examples.explanation: A sequence of jumps can reach the last index.

constraints: The array contains at least one non-negative value.

title: Clone Graph
summary: Deep-copy a graph while preserving its nodes and neighbor relationships.

prompt.description: Given a reference to a node in a connected undirected graph, create and return a deep copy of the entire graph.

examples.output: A deep copy with the same adjacency
examples.explanation: Every original node and edge is reproduced with new nodes.

constraints: The graph may contain cycles.
Node values are unique.

title: Course Schedule
summary: Detect whether course prerequisites contain a directed cycle.

prompt.description: Given a course count and prerequisite pairs, determine whether all courses can be completed.

examples.explanation: Course 0 can be taken before course 1.

constraints: A pair [a, b] means b must be completed before a.
Prerequisites may form cycles.

title: Pacific Atlantic Water Flow
summary: Find cells from which water can flow to both opposite ocean borders.

prompt.description: Given a height grid, return all cells from which water can flow to both the Pacific and Atlantic edges. Water can move to a neighboring cell of equal or lower height.

examples.explanation: Each listed cell has a downhill or level route to both oceans.

constraints: The grid is non-empty.
Return each qualifying coordinate once.

title: Number of Islands
summary: Count connected land components in a grid.

prompt.description: Given a grid of land ('1') and water ('0'), count the islands. Land connects horizontally or vertically.

examples.explanation: There are three separate connected groups of land.

constraints: The grid may be rectangular.
Diagonal adjacency does not connect land.

title: Longest Consecutive Sequence
summary: Find the longest run of consecutive values without sorting.

prompt.description: Given an unsorted integer array, return the length of the longest sequence of consecutive values. Values need not be adjacent in the input.

examples.explanation: The sequence 1, 2, 3, 4 has length 4.

constraints: Aim for O(n) time.

title: Alien Dictionary
summary: Infer a character ordering from words sorted in an unknown alphabet.

prompt.description: Given a sorted list of words from an unknown alphabet, return a valid ordering of its characters, or an empty string if the ordering is invalid or impossible.

examples.explanation: The word order implies a consistent precedence between characters.

constraints: A character order must respect every adjacent-word distinction.
A longer word cannot precede its own strict prefix.

title: Graph Valid Tree
summary: Determine whether an undirected graph is connected and acyclic.

prompt.description: Given n nodes labeled 0 through n-1 and undirected edges, determine whether those edges form a valid tree.

examples.explanation: All nodes are connected and the graph has no cycle.

constraints: A valid tree is connected and contains no cycles.

title: Number of Connected Components in an Undirected Graph
summary: Count the disconnected groups of vertices.

prompt.description: Given n vertices and undirected edges, return the number of connected components.

examples.explanation: The vertices form two connected groups.

constraints: Vertices are labeled from 0 through n-1.

title: Insert Interval
summary: Insert a range into sorted, non-overlapping intervals and merge as needed.

prompt.description: Given sorted non-overlapping intervals and one new interval, insert it and merge any overlaps. Return the resulting intervals in order.

examples.explanation: The new range overlaps with [1, 3].

constraints: Input intervals are sorted by start.
Input intervals do not overlap.

title: Non-overlapping Intervals
summary: Remove as few ranges as possible to leave a non-overlapping set.

prompt.description: Given intervals, return the minimum number that must be removed so the remaining intervals do not overlap.

examples.explanation: Removing [1, 3] leaves non-overlapping intervals.

constraints: Intervals that touch at an endpoint do not overlap.

title: Meeting Rooms
summary: Check whether any scheduled meetings overlap.

prompt.description: Given meeting time intervals, return whether a person can attend every meeting without conflicts.

examples.explanation: The first meeting overlaps with both later meetings.

constraints: Each interval has a start earlier than its end.

title: Meeting Rooms II
summary: Find the minimum number of rooms needed for overlapping meetings.

prompt.description: Given meeting start and end times, return the minimum number of conference rooms required to hold all meetings.

examples.explanation: At most two meetings overlap at once.

constraints: Meeting intervals may be provided in any order.

title: Reverse Linked List
summary: Reverse the direction of every link in a singly linked list.

prompt.description: Given the head of a singly linked list, reverse the list and return its new head.

examples.explanation: The node order is reversed.

constraints: The list may be empty.

title: Linked List Cycle
summary: Detect whether following next pointers eventually revisits a node.

prompt.description: Given a linked-list head, return whether the list contains a cycle.

examples.explanation: The final node links back to the node at index 1.

constraints: The list may be empty.
Do not modify the list.

title: Merge Two Sorted Lists
summary: Merge two sorted linked lists into one sorted list.

prompt.description: Given the heads of two sorted singly linked lists, merge them into one sorted list and return its head.

examples.explanation: All nodes appear in ascending order.

constraints: Either input list may be empty.

title: Merge K Sorted Lists
summary: Combine many sorted linked lists into a single sorted list.

prompt.description: Given an array of k sorted linked lists, merge them into one sorted linked list and return its head.

examples.explanation: All values are merged in ascending order.

constraints: The array may contain empty lists.

title: Remove Nth Node From End of List
summary: Remove a node counted from the end of a singly linked list.

prompt.description: Given a list head and integer n, remove the nth node from the end and return the list head.

examples.explanation: The node with value 4 is removed.

constraints: n is valid for the list length.
Aim for one pass.

title: Reorder List
summary: Interleave nodes from the start and end of a linked list.

prompt.description: Reorder a list in place from L0 -> L1 -> ... -> Ln to L0 -> Ln -> L1 -> Ln-1 -> ... .

examples.explanation: Nodes from each end are alternated.

constraints: Do not change node values.
Reorder nodes in place.

title: Set Matrix Zeroes
summary: Zero entire rows and columns containing an original zero.

prompt.description: If a matrix cell is zero, set its entire row and column to zero. Perform the transformation in place.

examples.explanation: The middle row and column are set to zero.

constraints: Zeroes introduced during the transformation must not trigger extra changes.

title: Spiral Matrix
summary: Read matrix entries by spiraling inward from the outer boundary.

prompt.description: Given a matrix, return all its elements in clockwise spiral order.

examples.explanation: Traverse the perimeter before moving inward.

constraints: The matrix may have different numbers of rows and columns.

title: Rotate Image
summary: Rotate a square matrix clockwise without allocating another matrix.

prompt.description: Rotate an n by n matrix 90 degrees clockwise in place.

examples.explanation: The outer columns and rows rotate clockwise.

constraints: Modify the matrix in place.

title: Word Search
summary: Trace a word through adjacent cells without reusing a cell.

prompt.description: Given a character grid and a word, return whether the word can be formed by horizontally or vertically adjacent cells without using any cell more than once.

examples.explanation: A valid path visits adjacent cells and spells the word.

constraints: A cell may be used at most once in a path.

title: Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters
summary: Find the longest contiguous substring with all distinct characters.

prompt.description: Given a string, return the length of its longest substring containing no repeated characters.

examples.explanation: "abc" is a longest substring without repetition.

constraints: The input may be empty.

title: Longest Repeating Character Replacement
summary: Find the longest substring that can be made uniform with a limited number of replacements.

prompt.description: Given an uppercase string and integer k, return the length of the longest substring that can become all one character after replacing at most k characters.

examples.explanation: Replacing one character makes a length-four substring uniform.

constraints: The string contains uppercase English letters.
0 <= k <= text.length.

title: Minimum Window Substring
summary: Find the shortest substring containing every required character with multiplicity.

prompt.description: Given strings s and t, return the shortest substring of s containing every character in t, including repeated occurrences, or an empty string if none exists.

examples.explanation: "BANC" is the shortest substring containing A, B, and C.

constraints: The answer is unique if one exists.

title: Group Anagrams
summary: Group words that share the same character frequencies.

prompt.description: Given a list of strings, group together the strings that are anagrams of one another.

examples.explanation: Each group contains words with matching character counts.

constraints: The order of groups and their contents may vary.

title: Valid Palindrome
summary: Check whether normalized alphanumeric characters read the same in both directions.

prompt.description: Return whether a string is a palindrome after ignoring non-alphanumeric characters and letter case.

examples.input: text = "A man, a plan, a canal: Panama"
examples.explanation: Ignoring punctuation and case gives a palindrome.

constraints: An empty normalized string is a palindrome.

title: Longest Palindromic Substring
summary: Find the longest contiguous substring that reads identically in both directions.

prompt.description: Given a string, return its longest palindromic substring.

examples.explanation: "aba" is also a valid longest answer.

constraints: The string is non-empty.

title: Palindromic Substrings
summary: Count every contiguous substring that is a palindrome.

prompt.description: Given a string, return the number of its non-empty substrings that are palindromes.

examples.explanation: There are three single-character, two length-two, and one length-three palindromes.

constraints: Substrings are identified by their start and end positions.

title: Encode and Decode Strings
summary: Design a reversible encoding for a list of strings, including strings with delimiters.

prompt.description: Design encode and decode functions that convert a list of strings into one string and restore the original list exactly.

examples.explanation: The encoding must preserve boundaries and arbitrary string contents.

constraints: Strings may contain any characters.
Decoding must reverse the encoding without ambiguity.

title: Maximum Depth of Binary Tree
summary: Find the number of nodes on the longest root-to-leaf path.

prompt.description: Given the root of a binary tree, return its maximum depth.

examples.explanation: The deepest root-to-leaf paths contain three nodes.

constraints: An empty tree has depth 0.

title: Same Tree
summary: Compare two trees for identical structure and values.

prompt.description: Given the roots of two binary trees, return whether they have the same structure and equal values at every corresponding node.

examples.explanation: Both trees have matching values and structure.

constraints: Either tree may be empty.

title: Invert Binary Tree
summary: Swap the left and right subtrees at every node.

prompt.description: Given the root of a binary tree, invert it and return the root.

examples.explanation: Every node's left and right children are exchanged.

constraints: The tree may be empty.

title: Binary Tree Maximum Path Sum
summary: Find the highest-sum path between any two nodes in a binary tree.

prompt.description: Given a binary tree, return the maximum sum of values along any non-empty path. A path may start and end at any nodes.

examples.explanation: The path 2 -> 1 -> 3 has sum 6.

constraints: A path follows parent-child edges and contains at least one node.

title: Binary Tree Level Order Traversal
summary: Return node values grouped by their depth in the tree.

prompt.description: Given a binary tree root, return its values level by level from left to right.

examples.explanation: Each inner list contains one tree level.

constraints: An empty tree produces an empty result.

title: Serialize and Deserialize Binary Tree
summary: Design reversible operations that preserve a binary tree's structure and values.

prompt.description: Design serialize and deserialize operations that convert a binary tree to a string and reconstruct an equivalent tree.

examples.explanation: The encoding must retain both values and child structure.

constraints: The serialization format is your choice.
The deserialized tree must match the original.

title: Subtree of Another Tree
summary: Check whether one tree occurs as a structurally identical subtree of another.

prompt.description: Given roots of two binary trees, determine whether the second tree appears as a subtree of the first, with matching values and structure.

examples.explanation: The subtree rooted at the node with value 4 matches.

constraints: A tree is not a subtree if its values match but its structure differs.

title: Construct Binary Tree from Preorder and Inorder Traversal
summary: Rebuild a binary tree from its preorder and inorder traversals.

prompt.description: Given preorder and inorder traversals of a binary tree with unique values, construct and return the tree.

examples.explanation: The traversals identify the root and recursively partition each subtree.

constraints: Values are unique.
Both traversals describe the same tree.

title: Validate Binary Search Tree
summary: Validate that every node respects the full ancestor bounds of a BST.

prompt.description: Given a binary tree, determine whether it is a valid binary search tree with strictly ordered values.

examples.explanation: The value 4 is in the right subtree of 5 but is smaller than 5.

constraints: Each node must respect bounds imposed by all its ancestors.

title: Kth Smallest Element in a BST
summary: Use the ordering of a BST to locate its kth smallest value.

prompt.description: Given the root of a binary search tree and integer k, return the kth smallest value.

examples.explanation: The smallest value in the tree is 1.

constraints: 1 <= k <= number of nodes.

title: Lowest Common Ancestor of a Binary Search Tree
summary: Find the deepest node that is an ancestor of both given BST nodes.

prompt.description: Given a binary search tree and two nodes in it, return their lowest common ancestor.

examples.explanation: The root is the lowest node whose subtree contains both nodes.

constraints: Both queried nodes exist in the tree.

title: Implement Trie (Prefix Tree)
summary: Implement a prefix tree supporting insertion, exact lookup, and prefix lookup.

prompt.description: Implement a trie with insert(word), search(word), and startsWith(prefix) operations.

examples.explanation: The full word is present and the prefix begins a stored word.

constraints: Words contain lowercase English letters.

title: Design Add and Search Words Data Structure
summary: Support word insertion and searches where a dot matches any one letter.

prompt.description: Design a data structure with addWord and search operations. In a search pattern, '.' matches any single lowercase letter.

examples.explanation: The wildcard can match the first letter of an inserted word.

constraints: Words and patterns contain lowercase letters or '.'.
A dot matches exactly one character.

title: Word Search II
summary: Find all dictionary words that can be traced through adjacent board cells.

prompt.description: Given a character board and a list of words, return all words that can be formed from adjacent cells without reusing a cell within a word.

examples.explanation: Only "eat" can be traced through adjacent cells in this board.

constraints: Adjacency is horizontal or vertical.
A board cell cannot be reused within one word.

title: Find Median from Data Stream
summary: Maintain a changing set of values while supporting median queries.

prompt.description: Design a data structure with addNum and findMedian operations for a stream of integers.

examples.explanation: The median is the middle value, or the mean of two middle values.

constraints: At least one value exists when findMedian is called.

title: Top K Frequent Elements
summary: Return the k values that occur most often in an integer array.

prompt.description: Given an integer array and integer k, return the k most frequent values in any order.

examples.explanation: 1 occurs three times and 2 occurs twice.

constraints: The answer is unique.
Aim for better than sorting all distinct values when possible.
